items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Ory wasn't a reader, Jack Carey wasn't a reader

ctx.x: The question, Risley, I've had this formal education in playing trombone in concert bands, in marching bands. But I'm always playing set notes of music, something that somebody else has written for me. And I'm very enchanted by this Dixieland music where the trombone player seems to be making it up and improvising and playing things that aren't written. And the music is a very happy type of music, which I think is good for relaxation for lawyers, among other people. And I'm wondering, how do you play, what do you…

Well, at our time back there, you know, we wasn't much of a reader. Spellers, and the trombone, he didn't do much. Most of the time he had bass licks, you know. And then he had nod, then he'd have a little solo or something. But he didn't play trombone like those fellas. The most was a gift, and we done most sliding and faking on such an audible step, you see. We couldn't play no trombone like those boys were playing that they didn't know how. You see, and which was just mostly a gift. And most of us played from…

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: We whipped Ory's band on a parade.

ctx.x: Do you use shots on trumpet? Shots.

Did shots. Yeah. And the shots I had been playing second with. He knows everything, you know. He could play a mirror and everything. He said, I'm going to play something. And so they came up and knocked off and said, people didn't know the difference. They said, some people thought of the same band. He said, we didn't tell them no better. He said, now you just come on out, sir, and practice up until you bring your band up again. They allowed me to build up another good band. And I got David Jones and another…

Did they give cups sometimes? Like contests? A lot of people had one hander. Nice to see it. Anyway, you run those cups and all. We ripped them all. I was going to ask about the brass bands. If the tuxedo brass band marched on the street, the same fellows that played in the dance band, did you march on the street much?

No. Good role. Good role. No. Good role. No, it was good. But from what Roy is doing there now, Roy didn't get up to that. Roy got a little of everything on that from there now.
